summary: Source decomposition of the abstract completed-cohomology machinery from Calegari-Emerton's survey, read in full for its statements, together with Scholze's section 4.2 for the perfectoid comparison and the vanishing and codimension results it yields. Covered with nodes: the tower axioms and the two standing hypotheses (finite simplicial homotopy type, p-adic analytic G_0) that the source says are not removable; the four completed modules and the exact sequence separating the p-adic completion from the Tate module; finite generation over the Iwasawa algebra with the identification of the canonical and projective-limit topologies; the duality sequences (exact in characteristic zero, isomorphisms mod p) and the universal-coefficient sequences; the Hochschild-Serre descent spectral sequences; codimension and Iwasawa dimension with the torsion theorem; the Borel-Serre boundary tower; and Scholze's named comparison isomorphism with its tame-level convention. The dominant boundary is that the survey PROVES none of its main theorems: Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.16 are deferred to a paper that is not in the supplied library. Conjecture 1.5 is recorded as a conjecture, not an input.

nodes.title: The axioms on the tower, and the two standing hypotheses without which nothing is controlled
nodes.statement: Let G_0 be a profinite group with a countable basis of neighbourhoods of the identity consisting of normal open subgroups ... contained in G_r contained in ... contained in G_1 contained in G_0. Suppose given a tower of topological spaces ... -> X_r -> ... -> X_1 -> X_0, each with an action of G_0, such that (1) the maps X_{r+1} -> X_r are G_0-equivariant, and (2) G_r acts trivially on X_r and realizes X_r as a G_0/G_r-torsor over X_0 - in particular all the maps in the tower are FINITE COVERINGS. Two standing hypotheses are imposed from that point on: (a) each X_r is a manifold homotopic to a finite simplicial complex, which is what makes all four families of (co)homology groups finitely generated over the indicated coefficient ring and relates them by the appropriate duality; and (b) G_0 is a p-ADIC ANALYTIC group - the source says that without this 'it seems impossible to control the inverse limits involved in our constructions', and with it Lazard's theorem that Z_p[[G_0]] is noetherian plus Schneider-Teitelbaum's Banach-representation theory bring the limits under control. In the arithmetic application X_r = G(Q)\G(A)/A_infinity^o K_infinity^o G_r K^{infinity,p}, and the resulting modules carry not only the G_0-action but actions of the whole p-adic group G(Q_p), of a completed Hecke algebra T built from spherical Hecke operators at primes l different from p where G and the tame level K^{infinity,p} are unramified, and of the component group pi_0 = (A_infinity K_infinity)/(A_infinity^o K_infinity^o).

nodes.title: The four completed (co)homology modules, and the exact sequence separating the completion from the Tate module
nodes.statement: Having fixed p, define completed homology and cohomology by H-tilde_bullet = inverse limit over r of H_bullet(X_r, Z_p) and H-tilde^bullet = inverse limit over s of the direct limit over r of H^bullet(X_r, Z/p^s Z), with Borel-Moore and compactly supported variants H-tilde^BM_bullet = inverse limit over r of H^BM_bullet(X_r, Z_p) and H-tilde_c^bullet = inverse limit over s of the direct limit over r of H_c^bullet(X_r, Z/p^s Z). There are natural maps H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet. Define also H-hat^bullet = the p-adic completion of the direct limit over r of H^bullet(X_r, Z_p), and T_p H^bullet = the p-adic Tate module of that direct limit. Then there is an exact sequence 0 -> H-hat^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet -> T_p H^{bullet+1} -> 0 (1.1), stated in the source without proof. The p-adic completion kills the p-divisible part of the direct limit, while the Tate module sees only the torsion subgroup of that divisible part. Since T_p H^{bullet+1} is p-torsion free and p-adically complete, dualizing gives 0 -> Hom(T_p H^{bullet+1}, Z_p) -> Hom(H-tilde^bullet, Z_p) -> Hom(H-hat^bullet, Z_p) -> 0. The source then quotes Theorem 1.1(3) to identify the middle term with the p-torsion-free quotient of H-tilde_bullet; that consequence is recorded in the duality node (CC.3), because the atlas places Theorem 1.1(3) after CC.2. Remark 1.15: if the Z_p-cohomology of every X_r is p-torsion-free, or more generally of bounded exponent, the Tate-module term vanishes and H-hat^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: the order of the limits is not interchangeable: H-tilde^bullet is inverse limit over s of direct limit over r, and the two other objects H-hat and T_p H are obtained from the SAME direct limit by completion and by Tate module respectively

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1(3) and Theorem 1.16(3),(5): the exact sequences and isomorphisms relating completed homology and cohomology
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1(3): there are short exact sequences 0 -> Hom_cont(H-tilde_{bullet-1}, Q_p/Z_p) -> H-tilde^bullet -> Hom_cont(H-tilde_bullet, Z_p) -> 0 (as printed; see the reviewer note at the end: the first term must be read as Hom_cont(H-tilde_{bullet-1}[p^infinity], Q_p/Z_p)), where 'cont' means continuous for the canonical topology on the source and the evident (discrete or p-adic) topology on the target, and 0 -> Hom(H-tilde^{bullet+1}[p^infinity], Q_p/Z_p) -> H-tilde_bullet -> Hom(H-tilde^bullet, Z_p) -> 0, together with similar sequences relating H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet; these are compatible with the maps H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet. nodes.title: Codimension over a noncommutative Iwasawa algebra, and Theorem 1.4: completed homology is torsion outside the middle degree
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated left Z_p[[G_0]]-module M set E^bullet(M) = Ext^bullet(M, Z_p[[G_0]]), computed via the left module structure on Z_p[[G_0]] and converted back to a left module structure by the canonical anti-involution g -> g^{-1}; these modules are unchanged (up to natural isomorphism and forgetting) on replacing G_0 by an open subgroup. The CODIMENSION of M is the least i with E^i(M) nonzero; the IWASAWA DIMENSION is 1 + dim G_0 - codim M. In the mod p setting, for a finitely generated left F_p[[G_0]]-module M, E_{F_p}^bullet(M) = Ext^bullet(M, F_p[[G_0]]) and, regarding M as a Z_p[[G_0]]-module and applying Ext^bullet(M, -) to 0 -> Z_p[[G_0]] -> Z_p[[G_0]] -> F_p[[G_0]] -> 0 (multiplication by p), the short exact sequences 0 -> E^bullet(M) -> E_{F_p}^bullet(M) -> E^{bullet+1}(M) -> 0 show the F_p-codimension is one less than the codimension, so the Iwasawa dimension equals dim G_0 - codim_{F_p} M. Lemma 1.17: if M is finitely generated over Z_p[[G_0]] and p-TORSION FREE then codim M = codim_{F_p} M/pM. Theorem 1.4 (the main result of an earlier paper of the authors): if G is SEMI-SIMPLE then the modules H-tilde_n are TORSION Z_p[[G_0]]-modules, unless G(R) admits discrete series and n is the middle dimension (half the dimension of the X_r); in that case Hom(H-hat^n, Z_p), and hence H-tilde_n, has positive rank, while Hom(T_p H^{n+1}, Z_p) is torsion over Z_p[[G_0]]. Theorem 1.18: if M is finitely generated over F_p[[G_0]] with V = Hom_cont(M, F_p) the corresponding admissible smooth representation, and the Iwasawa dimension of M is d, then dim H^0(G_r, V) is asymptotic to lambda [G_0 : G_r]^{d/dim G_0} for some lambda > 0, while dim H^i(G_r, V) = O([G_0 : G_r]^{d/dim G_0}) for all i > 0.

nodes.title: The Borel-Serre boundary tower and its long exact sequences
nodes.statement: Each X_r embeds as an open subset of its Borel-Serre compactification X-bar_r; write dX_r = X-bar_r minus X_r for the boundary. As r varies the X-bar_r form a tower to which the completed (co)homology machinery applies, so one may define completed (co)homology spaces H-tilde_bullet(boundary) and H-tilde^bullet(boundary), and there are long exact sequences (1.2) ... -> H-tilde_bullet(boundary) -> H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde^BM_bullet -> H-tilde_{bullet-1}(boundary) -> ... and (1.3) ... -> H-tilde^{bullet-1}(boundary) -> H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet(boundary) -> ..., stated without proof. (Reviewer: the drafted '(d)' for the boundary is corrected to the source's boundary symbol; the source also describes the stratification of the boundary by proper parabolics P, a Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, and the induction formula (1.4) after a colimit over tame levels, at least for p odd - read, not decomposed.) Scholze's Corollary 4.2.2, for the compactly supported completed cohomology of a Shimura variety of Hodge type with tame level K^p contained in the level-N subgroup for some N >= 3 prime to p: the group H-tilde^i_{c, K^p}(Z/p^n Z) (and a fortiori with Z_p coefficients) VANISHES for i > d, where d = dim_C X_K. Corollary 4.2.3: for i > d one has H-tilde^{BM}_i = 0 and H-tilde^{BM}_d is p-torsion free; for i < d the codimension of H-tilde_i over the Iwasawa algebra is at least d - i. If the X_K are compact this gives all of the Calegari-Emerton Conjecture 1.5 in that case, except with non-strict instead of strict inequalities on the codimensions (Scholze prints 'here l_0 = d and q_0 = 0'). Reviewer correction: those values are swapped. With the survey's definitions l_0 = rank G_infinity - rank A_infinity K_infinity and q_0 = (d_R - l_0)/2, where d_R is the real dimension of X_r, only l_0 = 0 and q_0 = d (Scholze's d = dim_C) makes Corollary 4.2.3 match Conjecture 1.5 parts (1), (5) and (7); with l_0 = d and q_0 = 0, part (7) would say H-tilde_n = 0 for all n > 0. For G = Sp_2g the definitions give l_0 = 0 and q_0 = g(g+1)/2 = d directly. Scholze also points to the survey's Theorem 1.4 for the remaining part (2).

proofSteps: The survey records the boundary tower and its long exact sequences.

Scholze's Corollary 4.2.2 (statement printed p. 1023, proof pp. 1023-1024) reduces to n = 1 by long exact sequences, then to showing that H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(F_p) tensor O_C/p is almost zero for i > d: for a nontrivial F_p-vector space V, V tensor O_C/p is flat over O_C/p and nonzero, so if it is killed by the maximal ideal of O_C it is 0. By Theorem 4.2.1 it suffices that H^i(X*_{K^p}, F) = 0 for i > d for EVERY abelian sheaf F on the spectral space X*_{K^p}. A cofiltered inverse limit of spectral spaces of cohomological dimension <= d along spectral maps again has cohomological dimension <= d (constructible sheaves come from a finite stage), and |X*_{K^p}| = lim |X*_{K_pK^p}|, so it is enough that each X*_{K_pK^p} has cohomological dimension <= d. For that Scholze cites de Jong-van der Put [41, Prop. 2.5.8], or writes the space as the inverse limit of the spaces underlying its formal models (each of dimension <= d) and uses Grothendieck's bound for noetherian spectral spaces; neither import was read.

Corollary 4.2.3's first two assertions follow from Corollary 4.2.2 together with Theorem 1.1(iii) of the survey (Scholze's [17] is the published version, London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 393, 2012; the library copy is the author's file). Reviewer: this step needs the torsion submodule in the first duality sequence (see the duality node). The codimension bound is proved by a minimal-counterexample argument using the Poincare duality spectral sequence E_2^{jk} = E^j(H-tilde_k) => H-tilde^{BM}_{2d-j-k}, Venjakob's results [63] (if X has codimension c then E^j(X) = 0 for j < c, E^c(X) has codimension exactly c, E^j(X) has codimension >= j for j > c) and the good behaviour of codimension in short exact sequences.

nodes.statement: In Scholze's section 4.2 the compactly supported completed cohomology used is H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(Z/p^n Z) = direct limit over K_p of H^i_c(X_{K_p K^p}, Z/p^n Z), with (G, D) of Hodge type, a fixed embedding into (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}), and the standing convention that the tame level K^p is contained in the level-N subgroup of G'(A_f^p) for some N >= 3 prime to p. Theorem 4.2.1: there is a natural isomorphism of almost-O_C-modules H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(Z/p^n Z) tensor_{Z/p^n Z} O_C^a/p^n = H^i(X^*_{K^p}, I^{+a}_{X^*_{K^p}}/p^n), where the right-hand cohomology is computed on the topological space X^*_{K^p} and I_{X^*_{K^p}} is the ideal sheaf of the boundary with I^+ its intersection with O^+; moreover, for K_1^p contained in K_2^p, the isomorphisms commute with the pullback maps and with the trace maps (two commutative diagrams). Scholze notes that the right-hand side is the cohomology of the sheaf of p-adic cusp forms modulo p^n of infinite level. gaps.title: Lemma 1.17's printed proof overstates an isomorphism
gaps.detail: Verified: Lemma 1.17 (p. 14) and its proof, which asserts E^bullet(M)/pE^bullet(M) = E^bullet_{F_p}(M/pM) for finitely generated p-torsion-free M. Reviewer check: reducing Hom(P_bullet, Z_p[[G_0]]) modulo p gives only 0 -> E^i(M)/p -> E^i_{F_p}(M/pM) -> E^{i+1}(M)[p] -> 0. For G_0 = Z_p and M = (p, T) in Z_p[[T]], the degree-0 cokernel is E^1(M)[p] = F_p. The lemma holds exactly when E^c(M) is p-torsion-free for c = codim M. For G_0 = Z_p^k this follows from local duality (the associated primes of Ext^c(M, Lambda) are associated primes of M, and none contains p), but it was not checked for noncommutative G_0. Proposition 1.20 rests on the lemma. A related point: the short exact sequences 0 -> E^bullet(M) -> E^bullet_{F_p}(M) -> E^{bullet+1}(M) -> 0 on p. 14 hold with Ext over Z_p[[G_0]], while with Ext over F_p[[G_0]] Rees's lemma gives E^i_{F_p}(M) = E^{i+1}(M); the codimension conclusion is the same.
